desc:
WooCommerce plugin development is the work of turning your idea into a safe, installable plugin that follows WordPress coding standards. Ecom Swift LLC agrees the features in writing, builds and tests the plugin, then hands over the zip, the source code and short documentation.

## What is WooCommerce plugin development?

It is writing PHP, and sometimes JavaScript, that extends WooCommerce through its documented hooks and APIs rather than by changing core files. The finished plugin adds a feature such as a pricing rule, a product tab, a custom email or an admin report. It can be installed, updated and removed without leaving damage behind.

A good plugin behaves well in the background. It does not slow down pages, it does not clash with other plugins and it keeps customer data safe.

## Why does code quality matter in a WooCommerce plugin?

A plugin runs inside a store that takes real payments and holds real customer details. Unescaped output, missing permission checks or unsanitized input can open security holes. A badly written plugin can also load heavy queries on every page, which makes the whole store slow.

Updates are the other risk. WooCommerce, WordPress and PHP change often. A plugin built on undocumented tricks breaks at the next release, and the owner pays again to repair it. Clean, standard code is cheaper to maintain over time.

## How a well-built plugin supports your business

For a store owner, a plugin matters because it removes manual work or adds something customers can use. For a developer or agency, it may be a product that other stores install. In both cases, trust is the real asset. Store owners keep plugins that are stable and that stay out of their way.

Compatibility with current order storage and the block-based checkout also protects your reach. A plugin that works only with older setups loses users as stores move forward.

## What a great WooCommerce plugin includes

- One agreed feature set, written down before coding starts.
- WooCommerce hooks and filters used as documented.
- A settings page inside the WooCommerce admin.
- Input sanitized, output escaped, and permission checks on every action.
- Translation-ready text, so other languages can be added.
- Compatibility with High-Performance Order Storage when orders are involved.
- Clean removal of stored data on uninstall.
- Block checkout support when the feature touches checkout.
- Automated tests for the core logic, in higher packages.
- A readme and user documentation, plus the source code.

## What we do

We begin with a short specification: what the plugin does, which screens it adds, what data it stores and what should happen in edge cases. You approve it before development begins. This protects both sides from misunderstandings.

We then build the plugin in steps, testing on a staging copy with the current WooCommerce release and recent PHP versions. We check how it behaves with a default theme and with yours. When the plugin is ready, we deliver an installable zip, the source and a short guide. The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in the number of features, admin screens, emails, tests and documentation, and in the length of the bug-fix period.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Describe who will use the plugin and what they should be able to do.
- Share examples, sketches or competitor behavior you like.
- Decide early whether the plugin is private or will be published.
- Review the specification carefully before approving it.
- Test the finished plugin on a staging site first.

**Avoid:**
- Changing the scope during the build without agreeing the change.
- Asking for a plugin that edits WooCommerce core files.
- Skipping the uninstall behavior, which leaves orphaned data.
- Letting several developers add code to the same plugin without review.
- Installing the first version on a live store before testing.

## Who this service is for

This service suits a store owner with a specific business rule that no existing plugin handles. It suits an agency that needs a clean plugin for a client project. It also suits a founder who wants to publish a plugin for other stores and needs a solid first version.

## What we need from you

Send a plain description of the plugin, even a sketch or a few bullet points. Tell us your WooCommerce setup, your theme and any plugins it must work with. We never need your password. Access is given as a developer, staff or collaborator user, or through a staging site. Once you order, we reply with questions and the written specification.
